prose_evidence.text_as_printed: From my perspective there are two valid styles of play for a Blood Mage, which roughly correlate to:

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: The Maximized Blood Mage The Conservative Blood Mage
prose_evidence.source_html:
The Maximized Blood Mage
The Conservative Blood Mage

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: A Conservative Blood Mage in my view is one that spends most of their time in 'Sanguine Focus' stance and utilized direct healing spells as their primary form of healing.
prose_evidence.source_html: A Conservative Blood Mage in my view is one that spends most of their time in 'Sanguine Focus' stance and utilized direct healing spells as their primary form of healing.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: While this is a valid way to play, there is no reason to play a Blood Mage if this is your preferred style. The Cleric excels at this style of play and has more tools in their toolbox to be better at it.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: And thats all I really have to say about that…

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Lets move on to the meat of this article, the Maximized Blood Mage
prose_evidence.source_html: Lets move on to the meat of this article, the Maximized Blood Mage

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: A Maximized Blood Mage is a player that EMBRACES the unique characteristics of this class and tries to emphasize them at every opportunity. That means the Life Tap healing spells are your preferred method of healing and Focus of Gelenia is your preferred Stance. It means you like to pump out major DPS as you keep your group alive. It means you live vicariously as your health bar rubber bands all over the place during the course of battle. It means you embrace the challenge this class has to offer!

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Why play a Maximized Blood Mage? These are the compelling reasons from my perspective
prose_evidence.source_html: Why play a Maximized Blood Mage? These are the compelling reasons from my perspective

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: no desire to play a 'standard healer'
prose_evidence.source_html: • no desire to play a 'standard healer'

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: playing a character with vampiric abilities appeals to your inner gamer geek
prose_evidence.source_html: • playing a character with vampiric abilities appeals to your inner gamer geek

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: You love to DPS, and you love to play a healer, but you don't have time to play two different classes!

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: your nature is to seek out the most challenging and difficult classes in any MMO

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: the COOL factor

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: And maybe some reasons to avoid the Maximized Blood Mage style:
prose_evidence.source_html: And maybe some reasons to avoid the Maximized Blood Mage style:

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Its hard! Being 'OK' at a Cleric is perfectly fine in most situations. Being 'OK' at playing a very aggressive style of Blood Mage is a recipe for disaster.
prose_evidence.source_html: • Its hard! Being 'OK' at a Cleric is perfectly fine in most situations. Being 'OK' at playing a very aggressive style of Blood Mage is a recipe for disaster.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: You panic when your health gets low. For a Maximized Blood Mage, your health bar fluctuates wildly. You live on the edge of disaster. If that doesn't appeal to you, stay away.
prose_evidence.source_html: • You panic when your health gets low. For a Maximized Blood Mage, your health bar fluctuates wildly. You live on the edge of disaster. If that doesn't appeal to you, stay away.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Resists impact your ability to heal…major bummer

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: you don't solo as well as some other classes

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: you don't like the color red. Just about every spell effect we have involves some hazy red stuff floating around :/

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Ok by now I've either convinced you that playing an aggressive style of Blood Mage is really cool or somthing to be avoided at all costs. If you are the latter, then thanks for reading down to here! Bye!

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: If you are the former then let me get into a discussion of the actual mechanics of playing a Maximized Blood Mage:
prose_evidence.source_html: If you are the former then let me get into a discussion of the actual mechanics of playing a Maximized Blood Mage:

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: First up…Hotkeys & Macros.
prose_evidence.source_html: First up…Hotkeys & Macros.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: If you are a mouse clicker then don't bother applying at the Maximized Blood Mage School of Insanity. The Vanguard UI slow and inefficient in the best of times and this play style requires too much precision to be effective using mouse clicks to select spells & abilities. Now, assuming you agree with this, lets move on to Stance Dancing.
prose_evidence.source_html: If you are a mouse clicker then don't bother applying at the Maximized Blood Mage School of Insanity. The Vanguard UI slow and inefficient in the best of times and this play style requires too much precision to be effective using mouse clicks to select spells & abilities. Now, assuming you agree with this, lets move on to Stance Dancing.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: I don't know where it originated, but I first heard this term in WoW and it described a style of warrior play as they hopped between different battle stances.
prose_evidence.source_html: I don't know where it originated, but I first heard this term in WoW and it described a style of warrior play as they hopped between different battle stances.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: For a Blood Mage, stance dancing means every time you cast a Life Type style heal or Direct Damage spell, you put yourself in Focus of Gelenia stance for the 25% bonus, and when you cast a direct heal (hey…it happens) you shift your stance to Sanguine Focus.
prose_evidence.source_html: For a Blood Mage, stance dancing means every time you cast a Life Type style heal or Direct Damage spell, you put yourself in Focus of Gelenia stance for the 25% bonus, and when you cast a direct heal (hey…it happens) you shift your stance to Sanguine Focus.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Sound complicated? Nah, its trivial. Fortunately in Vanguard Stance Dancing does not fire the Global Cooldown, which means you can macro the stance changes. For example to make a Despoil macro:

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Now the macro stuff is useful but what this means is that because as a Maximized Blood Mage you cast Lifetap and DD style spells 90% of the time, that means you are in Focus of Gelenia stance 90% of the time which of course means you have 5% of your health ticking away constantly. Out of combat this is no big deal as your natural regen off sets it.
prose_evidence.source_html: Now the macro stuff is useful but what this means is that because as a Maximized Blood Mage you cast Lifetap and DD style spells 90% of the time, that means you are in Focus of Gelenia stance 90% of the time which of course means you have 5% of your health ticking away constantly. Out of combat this is no big deal as your natural regen off sets it.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: In combat however, it is a big deal and it means you MUST watch your health and use Despoil occasionally to top it off. If you are not on top of your game (and face it no one can be in top form 100% of the time) its easy to let your health slip too low and then a Despoil resist means disaster. Don't let this happen. If you are tired and not playing your best, switch to Unfocused or Sanguine Focus stances and stay there (which of course means you need a new set of hotkeys so you don't auto-switch)

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Why is LifeTap spells so core to this style? The key advantages are:
prose_evidence.source_html: Why is LifeTap spells so core to this style? The key advantages are:

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: DPS DPS DPS. In a tough dungeon you probably don't want to take the actual time to cast Burning Cyst (our dedicated Direct Damage spell). Too many bad things can happen while you are casting a 3 second spell that has no healing component. Chain casting lifetaps allows you to fulfill your duties as a healer and output some decent DPS.
prose_evidence.source_html: • DPS DPS DPS. In a tough dungeon you probably don't want to take the actual time to cast Burning Cyst (our dedicated Direct Damage spell). Too many bad things can happen while you are casting a 3 second spell that has no healing component. Chain casting lifetaps allows you to fulfill your duties as a healer and output some decent DPS.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Aggro control. The Lifetap heals just basically generate no aggro. I mean its just insanely hard to pull any type of aggro using the lifetap heals. They are awesome in this regard. And because the Blood Mage is so squishy, this is a good thing. Basically the only time I pull aggro is if I have to use a Direct Heal, which is all the more reason to avoid them.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Its easy to see why Maximized Blood Mage play requires the use of Focus of Gelenia! The bonus to damage and the free blood union points make us exponentially more effective.
prose_evidence.source_html: Its easy to see why Maximized Blood Mage play requires the use of Focus of Gelenia! The bonus to damage and the free blood union points make us exponentially more effective.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Only the Maximized Blood Mage can chain cast 270 point heals and draw no aggro even in a big fight with lots of adds. Try doing that with Infuse Health and you will not only run out of energy and do absolutely ZERO DPS but you'll draw every add over to you to pound you into a wet red spot on the floor.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: The other cool aspect of this is that Maximized Blood Mages can focus 100% on accumulating +Spell Damage gear and it enhances BOTH our Heals and DPS
prose_evidence.source_html: The other cool aspect of this is that Maximized Blood Mages can focus 100% on accumulating +Spell Damage gear and it enhances BOTH our Heals and DPS

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: But it doesn't stop there! NO WAY! At level 14 Blood Mages get another excellent spell called Scarring Pact. This is a bond you can form with a party member that splits incoming damage with them. They are granted a whopping 15% damage mitigation buff, but the cost is you take damage every time they are hit. This makes a VERY NOTICEABLE difference in how well the tank can mitigate damage…its awesome!

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: However, it also makes a VERY NOTICEABLE difference in how fast your health drops. Not only is Focus of Gelenia draining your health every few seconds, you are sharing damage with the main tank! Only an insane player would do such a thing! YEA BABY! Thats why you are attracted to the Maximized Blood Mage and you've read all this way down…you are a little nutty to begin with.

Not necessarily a big deal unless you get an unlucky run of the resists. If your health is dropping fast and you get a Despoil resist…well bad things can happen.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Synergy with other healers - Aggressive manipulation of your own health bar can sometimes stress out the other (if there are any) healers in your group. My recommendation in any multi-healer group is to set up heal assignments and agree not to cross heal unless you see health bars drop below 40%. Make sure the other healers know that YOU are responsible for your own health bar.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Mind Control - Another tool we get at level 14 is a form of Charm that lasts for 15 seconds. In my opinion while its a cool toy, it doesn't synergize well with the Maximized Blood Mage playstyle. The reason is that it is GUARANTEED AGGRO once the charm breaks. Maximized Blood Mages need to avoid aggro generating spells as much as possible.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Resists - No other healing class has RESISTS as a major factor in their healing effectiveness. SIGIL - PLEASE make the Union of Blood series of spells have a Lifetap specific resist debuff associated with it, so if we open with UoB then our subsequent lifetap spells are much less likely to be resisted.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Offensive Target Death - Another serious gotcha. If your Offensive Target dies while you are casting your Entwinging Vein or Despoil it has no effect. You must be quick to react if your offensive target dies while you are casting a lifetap heal. This problem is magnified by the relatively small amount of feedback the Vanguard UI provides on these type of events. SIGIL PLEASE give us an audible signal when our BU is broken due to target death.
